props.title: Waxwork

sections.content: Waxwork brilliantly blends horror-comedy with meta-commentary on classic monster movies. Director Anthony Hickox crafts an ingenious premise: a mysterious waxwork exhibition that serves as a portal into various horror scenarios. Like The Monster Squad (1987) and Night of the Demons (1988), it captures that specific late-80s horror vibe where practical effects reign supreme and genre mashups were hitting their stride. The film's clever structure allows it to pay homage to multiple horror subgenres while maintaining its own unique identity.

sections.content: The film's greatest strength lies in its anthology-like structure, reminiscent of Creepshow (1982) but with a more cohesive through-line. Each waxwork tableau represents a different horror subgenre - vampires, werewolves, zombies - allowing Hickox to explore and lovingly parody multiple classic monster movie tropes. The practical effects by Bob Keen's team rival contemporary works like Hellraiser (1987) and The Evil Dead II (1987), particularly in the werewolf transformation sequences.

The film's meta aspects predate Scream (1996) by nearly a decade, with characters who are aware of horror movie conventions but still fall victim to them. Zach Galligan (fresh from Gremlins (1984)) and Deborah Foreman bring a perfect balance of camp and genuine fear to their performances, grounding the increasingly bizarre scenarios in relatable reactions. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

movies.title: From Beyond
movies.slug: Lovecraftian horror about scientists opening doorways to other dimensions

sections.content: Waxwork influenced later horror-comedies that played with multiple subgenres, like Cabin in the Woods (2012) and Tales from the Crypt: Demon Knight (1995). Its blend of humor and horror, along with its "portal to other worlds" concept, can be seen reflected in everything from Evil Dead II (1987) to modern anthology series like American Horror Story (2011-present).
